Al Jazeera (AFP/Reuters) | datePublished: 2026-10-23T23:10:54Z | dateModified: 2026-10-24T04:50:23Z

Typhoon Champi has killed one person and injured more than 350 (Guardian reports over 500) in Taiwan after sweeping past the island's northeast on Friday, toppling trees, triggering brief flooding, disrupting power lines and forcing more than 5,000 people to evacuate their homes.

Emergency crews were sent out on Saturday to restore power to about 56,000 households still without electricity. Most shops in northern and central Taiwan stayed shut for a second day. Taiwan's Ministry of Transportation and Communications said 259 flights were cancelled on Saturday, down from almost 1,000 on Friday.

Champi was briefly a super typhoon with winds of nearly 300km/h (186mph) but has weakened; the US Joint Typhoon Warning Center reported maximum winds of 185km/h on Friday. The storm is forecast to drop up to 900mm (35 inches) of rain between Thursday and Saturday, with the northeast hit hardest, before heading on towards China and Japan, where it is forcing further flight cancellations.

Cross-ref: Guardian (24 Oct, 02:22 GMT) "Typhoon Champi kills one and injures more than 500 in Taiwan as it heads to China"; NBC News also reported ~1,000 flights cancelled ahead of landfall.
